description: Replace the large-shape 4096 base factor bottleneck with a coarse cooperative two-level factorization: use a small number of cluster-resident supernodes, graph-captured or fused panel waves, tensor-core TRSM/SYRK, and explicit next-panel lookahead while retaining the donor's lower-only recursive outer algorithm.

Replaced the monolithic 4096 POTRF with a coarse two-level 2048+2048 factor: compact cuSOLVER leaves, direct cuBLAS TRSM for the off-diagonal supernode, FP16/tcgen05 lower rank-k, and lower-quadrant assembly. Full validation and fresh-input guards passed. Full-grid metric was 842.560 us; target large cells measured n8192=6017.361 us, n16384=15352.952 us, and n32768=42769.688 us.

Split each 4096 base into four 1024 compact POTRF supernodes with direct TRSM and tcgen05 triangular rank-k after every panel. Build and official/fresh validation passed, but benchmark correctness failed for all three large shapes with NaN/Inf output (n8192, n16384, n32768); non-target cells completed before the failure.

Kept the two 2048 compact factor leaves and direct TRSM, but replaced FP16 conversion/rank-k with a direct FP32-input tcgen05 update for the second supernode. Build and official/fresh validation passed; benchmark correctness again produced NaN/Inf for n8192, n16384, and n32768, so the coarse TF32 update path does not preserve the large-shape factorization contract as wired.

Kept the two 2048 compact POTRF leaves and direct TRSM, replacing the half-convert triangular rank-k with an in-place FP32 torch.addmm Schur update. Full validation/fresh guard and all benchmark cells passed. Aggregate was 841.386 us, with large cells n8192=6032.210 us, n16384=15396.541 us, and n32768=42839.061 us; this was 1.174 us lower aggregate than the half-update two-level trial amid unrelated-cell noise, while target cells were slightly higher.

Explored coarse replacements for the 4096 base factor while retaining the donor's lower-only outer recursion. Trial 0 used two compact 2048 POTRF leaves, direct TRSM, and FP16/tcgen05 rank-k: all checks passed at 842.560 us, with n8192/16384/32768 at 6017.361/15352.952/42769.688 us. Four 1024 supernodes and a two-level direct TF32 tcgen05 update both passed small validation but produced NaN/Inf on all large benchmark shapes and were logged. The final two-level variant used an FP32 in-place GEMM Schur update and passed all checks at a brief-best 841.386 us, with large cells 6032.210/15396.541/42839.061 us. The donor remains faster at 724.140 us and 4429.579/12008.706/36367.713 us. Final nsys capture was attempted through the wrapper but generated no report. Open directions include a custom cooperative 4096 panel kernel with device-side dependencies instead of library leaf launches, a graph-captured fixed-pointer two-level wave with correct capture setup, triangular-only FP32 tcgen05 updates that preserve the lower contract, and explicit overlap of the next 2048 POTRF with the current outer panel update.

Continue the large-shape factor direction from the retained donor: implement the unexplored fixed-pointer graph-captured two-level wave with correct capture setup and test explicit next-leaf POTRF overlap with the current outer update. Keep Schur updates FP32-stable and lower-triangular; profile the parent or first viable variant before choosing further structural changes.

Continue the large-shape factor direction from the retained donor: implement the unexplored fixed-pointer graph-captured two-level wave with correct capture setup and test explicit next-leaf POTRF overlap with the current outer update. Keep Schur updates FP32-stable and lower-triangular; profile the parent or first viable variant before choosing further structural changes.

Added a warmed fixed-pointer CUDA graph for the two-2048-leaf factor wave, direct TRSM, FP32 in-place GEMM Schur update, and the retained outer lower-only recursion. Build passed, but the leaderboard banned-text gate rejected a newly added comment containing the literal forbidden queue term before execution; logged before fixing the source text.

Fixed the banned source text and ran the warmed fixed-pointer graph for the complete large-shape two-leaf factor/outer recursion. The graph captures lower copy, two compact 2048 POTRF leaves, direct TRSM, FP32 in-place GEMM Schur update, outer direct/recursive solves, and lower-only rank-k on stable pointers. Full validation/fresh guard and all 15 cells passed at 812.782 us. Target cells were n8192=4839.282 us, n16384=12981.912 us, n32768=38272.097 us, improving the uncaptured FP32 two-level trial by 1193/2415/4567 us while remaining above the monolithic donor by 410/973/1904 us.

Captured an explicit lookahead schedule: update the next 4096 diagonal in FP32, publish an event, factor its two 2048 leaves on a secondary queue while the origin queue applies rectangular and far-trailing FP32 GEMM updates, then rejoin before the next panel solve. Build and official/fresh validation passed. Benchmark n8192 was correct but slow at 10612.589 us; n16384 and n32768 failed lower-triangular reconstruction (relative residual 0.249/0.725), showing the hand-partitioned outer Schur updates did not preserve the donor's triangular update semantics.

Removed the host-wide synchronize between warmup and capture while retaining the correct fixed-pointer two-leaf graph and FP32 lower-path Schur update. Full validation/fresh guard and all cells passed at a brief-best 812.451 us. Large cells were n8192=4842.043 us, n16384=12978.017 us, and n32768=38241.580 us; differences versus the synchronized capture were +2.761/-3.895/-30.517 us.

Continuation restored donor 96be23f4 and implemented the fixed-pointer graph-captured two-level wave with warmed library handles, two compact 2048 POTRF leaves, direct TRSM, FP32 in-place Schur update, and the donor's lower-only outer recursion. After logging a banned-comment validation failure, the viable synchronized capture passed all checks at 812.782 us with n8192/16384/32768=4839.282/12981.912/38272.097 us. Removing host synchronization retained correctness and reached a brief-best 812.451 us with 4842.043/12978.017/38241.580 us. Parent ncu and viable-variant nsys profiling were both attempted through the required wrapper; the former matched no kernels and the latter generated no report. Explicit event-driven next-factor overlap was also implemented and measured: n8192 was correct but 10612.589 us, while n16384/n32768 failed lower reconstruction because the rectangular/far Schur partition did not match the triangular donor update; that failure is committed and logged. The fixed-pointer capture remains ~410/969/1874 us above the monolithic donor on the three target cells. Open directions include capturing the monolithic 4096 donor wave itself, a lower-triangular FP32 update kernel that can expose independent next-diagonal and far-trailing regions without full GEMM semantics, and device-epoch lookahead inside one cooperative kernel rather than cross-queue library overlap.

Continue from the faster monolithic donor, not the two-leaf branch: capture the existing 4096 POTRF/TRSM/lower-update wave on stable pointers, then introduce lookahead only through a lower-triangular FP32 update kernel that cleanly separates next-diagonal and far-trailing regions. Avoid cross-queue full-GEMM partitioning; preserve the donor triangular semantics exactly.

Avoid cross-queue full-GEMM partitioning; preserve the donor triangular semantics exactly.

Captured the retained donor's existing stable-pointer large wave without changing its math: lower copy, monolithic 4096 cuSOLVER POTRF, direct/recursive TRSM, FP16-input FP32-accumulating lower-triangular rank-k, and final lower factor copy. Full validation/fresh guard and all cells passed at 812.429 us. Large cells were n8192=4844.767 us, n16384=12981.310 us, and n32768=38223.306 us; graph replay removed Python/launch overhead but remained above the uncaptured donor's earlier 4429.579/12008.706/36367.713 measurements.

Added dedicated FP32-input/FP32-accumulating CuTe triangular rank-k operations: one standard lower scheduler for the next 4096 diagonal and one offset lower scheduler skipping its first 36 cluster tiles for cross/far trailing regions. No upper tiles or full GEMM partitioning were used. Build and official/fresh validation passed; n8192 benchmark was correct at 4880.138 us, but n16384/n32768 produced NaN/Inf, indicating the compiled FP32 region updater's layout or scheduler contract is not yet correct for taller panels.

This continuation started from retained monolithic donor 96be23f4. Capturing its unchanged stable-pointer lower copy, 4096 cuSOLVER POTRF, recursive/direct TRSM, FP16-input FP32-accumulating lower-only rank-k, and factor copy passed all checks at 812.429 us, with n8192/16384/32768=4844.767/12981.310/38223.306 us. I then implemented a dedicated FP32 triangular region updater: a normal lower scheduler for the next 4096 diagonal and an offset lower scheduler that skips exactly its 36 cluster tiles and covers remaining cross/far lower tiles, avoiding upper writes and full-GEMM partitioning. It built and passed official/fresh validation; n8192 was correct at 4880.138 us, but n16384/n32768 produced NaN/Inf, so the tall-panel layout/scheduler contract requires correction. That failure is committed/logged, and the branch is restored to the viable monolithic capture ef0928b9b824a22cae50f36db9d7bf24fc6ed849. Open directions include compiling separate fixed-shape FP32 triangular operations for each trailing size rather than one dynamic tall-panel kernel, validating panel leading dimensions independently, and exposing a device completion epoch from the next-diagonal tile subset before adding factor lookahead.
